metadata.title: Paclitaxel Monotherapy 80mg/m² Day 1, 8, 15 and 22 – 28 Day
metadata.indication: Metastatic breast carcinoma; second-line metastatic ovarian cancer; relapsed or refractory small-cell lung cancer; or second-line metastatic bladder cancer, according to the selected NCCP indication.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Encoded protocol · full source coverage review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: The protocol has executable SACTCheck content but has not yet completed the v0.68.0 full source fidelity review. Use the current NCCP source as authoritative.

metadata.schedule_summary: Paclitaxel on Days 1, 8, 15 and 22 of a 28-day cycle; a Days 1, 8 and 15 schedule may be selected by the consultant. Confirm your appointment plan.
metadata.source_retrieval_method: Fresh official PDF download; source dose tables visually inspected
source_conflicts: Printed platelets 90 belongs to both the 100% and intermediate rows; explicit review replaces automatic clearance.
Printed ANC .99–1 and bilirubin 1.25–1.26 / 2–2.01 gaps are surfaced without rounding.

Conventional paclitaxel SmPC generic retreatment, toxicity and premedication differs from NCCP weekly regimen. Retain source-specific pathways and reconcile the actual product/local policy; no automatic generic substitution.

clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding includes NCCP 00226 Version 9. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

indications.description: Treatment of metastatic breast carcinoma in patients who have failed or are not candidates for standard anthracycline-containing therapy.
Second-line chemotherapy for metastatic ovarian cancer after failure of standard platinum-containing therapy.
Relapsed or refractory small-cell lung cancer.
Second-line chemotherapy for metastatic bladder cancer.
Second-line treatment of metastatic ovarian cancer after platinum-containing therapy.
Advanced urothelial carcinoma treated with weekly paclitaxel where clinically appropriate.

previous_dose_reductions.label: Previous paclitaxel dose reductions
previous_dose_reductions.help: Two prior reductions trigger consultant review rather than an unlisted further automatic reduction.

off_label_consent_confirmed.label: Weekly off-label use discussed and hospital approval/consent confirmed
off_label_consent_confirmed.help: NCCP 00226 v9 flags all four listed weekly indications, including metastatic breast cancer, as outside the Irish licence. Confirm informed consent and hospital acknowledgement under local policy; this is not limited to the SCLC context. A blank answer is not confirmation.

ecog.label: ECOG performance status
ecog.help: NCCP 00226 eligibility specifies ECOG 0–2 for every listed indication. Record the assessed value; a blank answer does not establish eligibility.

output_templates.contraindicated: Do not administer paclitaxel under this protocol.
output_templates.discontinue: Discontinue paclitaxel and obtain treating-clinician review.
output_templates.delay_then_dose_reduce: Delay treatment and apply the encoded dose reduction after recovery.
output_templates.delay: Delay treatment until the protocol recovery criterion is met.
output_templates.withhold_then_reduce: Withhold treatment until recovery, then apply the encoded dose reduction.
output_templates.dose_reduce: A paclitaxel dose reduction is indicated.
output_templates.consultant_review: Consultant review is required before treatment.
output_templates.proceed_with_caution: Core criteria were assessed, but optional domains remain unassessed.
output_templates.proceed: No encoded hold or dose-modification criterion was triggered.

rule_engine.conflict_policy: Use the most restrictive applicable action.
rule_engine.missing_data_policy: Core and conditionally required data block completion. Optional missing data are reported as coverage gaps and are never inferred as normal.

rules.explanation: Known hypersensitivity is an exclusion. Do not administer paclitaxel under this protocol.
Breastfeeding is an exclusion. Do not administer paclitaxel under this protocol.
Severe hepatic impairment is an exclusion. Consultant review is required.
Baseline ANC is below the protocol eligibility threshold of 1.5 ×10⁹/L.
Delay treatment. After recovery, reduce paclitaxel by one dose level to 65 mg/m² and consider G-CSF.
Delay treatment. After recovery, reduce paclitaxel by one dose level to 50 mg/m² and consider G-CSF.
Delay treatment and obtain consultant review because a further standard dose level is not defined; consider G-CSF.
ANC below 0.5 ×10⁹/L independently requires treatment delay. Duration and current dose refine whether a dose reduction is also required.
Platelets below 70 ×10⁹/L independently require treatment delay. Current dose is needed only to determine the exact subsequent dose level.
Delay treatment. After recovery, reduce paclitaxel by one dose level to 65 mg/m² and consider G-CSF.
Delay treatment. After recovery, reduce paclitaxel by one dose level to 50 mg/m² and consider G-CSF.
Delay treatment and obtain consultant review because a further standard dose level is not defined; consider G-CSF.
ANC is below 0.5 ×10⁹/L but has not remained below this threshold for 7 days. Delay treatment; the mandatory one-level reduction criterion is not yet met.
Delay treatment. After recovery, reduce paclitaxel by one dose level to 65 mg/m².
Delay treatment. After recovery, reduce paclitaxel by one dose level to 50 mg/m².
Delay treatment and obtain consultant review because a further standard dose level is not defined.
ANC 0.5–0.99 ×10⁹/L and/or platelets 70 to below 90 ×10⁹/L: delay treatment and consider dose reduction at a subsequent cycle.
ANC and platelet thresholds meet the protocol row for 100% dosing.
Transaminases are at least 10 ×ULN and/or bilirubin is above 5 ×ULN. Paclitaxel is contraindicated by the hepatic table.
Use 50% of the original paclitaxel dose for bilirubin 2.01–5 ×ULN when transaminases are below 10 ×ULN.
Use 75% of the original paclitaxel dose for bilirubin 1.26–2 ×ULN when transaminases are below 10 ×ULN.
No hepatic dose reduction is triggered when transaminases are below 10 ×ULN and bilirubin is at or below 1.25 ×ULN.
Grade 3 or higher neuropathy or other non-haematological toxicity requires discontinuation under Table 4.
Grade 2 motor or sensory neuropathy: decrease paclitaxel by 10 mg/m².
Grade 2 neuropathy is present after two prior dose reductions. Discuss continuation with the treating clinician.

action.until: toxicity resolves to grade 1 or lower

rules.explanation: Hold treatment until the grade 2 non-haematological toxicity resolves to grade 1 or lower, then decrease subsequent doses by 10 mg/m².
The grade 2 non-haematological toxicity has resolved to grade 1 or lower. Decrease subsequent paclitaxel doses by 10 mg/m².
A grade 2 non-haematological toxicity occurred after two prior dose reductions. Discuss continuation with the treating clinician.
No adverse-event dose modification is triggered by the entered neuropathy and other-toxicity grades.

action.recommendation: Platelets exactly 90 ×10⁹/L appear in both the printed 100% and delay rows. Resolve this overlap with the treating consultant/pharmacist before dosing; no automatic full dose is supplied.

rules.explanation: Platelets exactly 90 ×10⁹/L appear in both the printed 100% and delay rows. Resolve this overlap with the treating consultant/pharmacist before dosing; no automatic full dose is supplied.

action.recommendation: ANC lies between the printed 0.99 and 1.0 boundaries. Do not round into a dose row; confirm the source interpretation.

rules.explanation: ANC lies between the printed 0.99 and 1.0 boundaries. Do not round into a dose row; confirm the source interpretation.

action.recommendation: Bilirubin lies in a decimal gap between the printed hepatic dose bands. No rounded 75% or 50% dose is calculated; obtain consultant/pharmacy interpretation.

rules.explanation: Bilirubin lies in a decimal gap between the printed hepatic dose bands. No rounded 75% or 50% dose is calculated; obtain consultant/pharmacy interpretation.

action.recommendation: Febrile neutropenia independently requires delay and a one-level reduction after recovery. Confirm the actual current dose before selecting 65 or 50 mg/m²; consider G-CSF.

rules.explanation: Febrile neutropenia independently requires delay and a one-level reduction after recovery. Confirm the actual current dose before selecting 65 or 50 mg/m²; consider G-CSF.

action.recommendation: Grade 2 neuropathy requires a 10 mg/m² reduction, but prior reductions must be checked before selecting the next dose. After two reductions, continuation needs consultant discussion.

rules.explanation: Grade 2 neuropathy requires a 10 mg/m² reduction, but prior reductions must be checked before selecting the next dose. After two reductions, continuation needs consultant discussion.

action.recommendation: Hold after grade 2 non-haematological toxicity until recovery to grade 1 or lower is confirmed. Establish current grade and previous reductions before selecting the subsequent 10 mg/m² reduction or consultant pathway.

rules.explanation: Hold after grade 2 non-haematological toxicity until recovery to grade 1 or lower is confirmed. Establish current grade and previous reductions before selecting the subsequent 10 mg/m² reduction or consultant pathway.

action.recommendation: Current grade 2 non-haematological toxicity independently requires withholding until grade 1 or lower, including after two previous reductions. A lower historical-grade entry does not override the current finding.
